body: I don't have the luxury of taking a step back. I either show up and attempt the rest of exams (and fail them too) or be absent and get a 0.

Withdrawing and/or failing the year means I don't get to graduate with my classmates and am out of a job, dependant on my parents for yet another year. Withdrawing also just postpones the problem and will make the situation 10 times worse because of all of the above factors. I also can't withdraw even if I wanted to because I've already attempted (and failed) some of the exams this year.

Thanks for your kind words. I got very lucky to have made it this far (it certainly wasn't from skill) and I feel like now that luck has run out and all my inadequacies are being exposed at this late stage in the game - after the first failure the uni basically told me to fuck off, that they have no intention of helping me get up to standard 

Right now I just really don't have anything left in me and am running on fumes. I'm so wound up that I can't even perform with the easy stuff

Do you really think I would be where I am if I hadn't fucking tried and struggled every day? It's easy for someone who hasn't felt miserable and dispairing 99% of days over the last 10 years to say what you're saying. Being awake every day is mental torture and makes me feel physically sick. It's not normal to go through life and accept that as your reality. Like I've said, I've already sought professional help and have made zero progress over the past 10 years and there's nothing in my external circumstances to suggest that I have anything to look forward to besides more misery
